attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, stated in his voice.

semantics.note: Keeps 'I don't think', the oligopoly scope and both stated causes. In context ('To be clear') this is a firm judgement, not graded confidence, so it is treated as a scored causal claim.

contract.note: The speaker gave no measure of 'worked' and no market or accounting basis. Testing at the post date with a Q2 2024 financial premise is an ordinary reading, and the contract rightly says losses alone cannot show failure or its cause.

evidence.note: Genuine CMA statement from April 2024 about competition risks. It is labelled company_disclosure but it is a regulator statement. It makes no finding that the control strategy succeeded or failed.
Microsoft's own disclosure of AI demand inside Azure growth. It does not isolate generative AI profit or loss and says nothing about whether control was achieved or why.

reviews.rationale: Nothing in the packet shows that the control strategy had failed or succeeded by August 2024. Nothing gives sector-wide losses against revenue, and nothing links returns to a market outcome. Neither the claimed failure nor its claimed cause is established or refuted.

attribution.note: Zitron asserts this as fact in his own post, as the reason in his 'because' clause.

semantics.note: The premise is asserted as fact, not hedged, so extracting it as a present-tense observation is faithful. Both parts are kept: financial losses and unsolved complex problems.

contract.note: Losses against revenue across providers in the latest reportable quarter is a fair plain reading. 'So much more' and 'complex problems' are undefined, so the result depends on the evaluator's reading.

evidence.note: Secondary summary of The Information's estimates for one provider (OpenAI): a full-year expense projection and annualized June revenue. It is not realized Q2 sector-wide data, so it cannot settle the comparison, though it points the same way as the claim.
Study of a deployment that predates the target quarter. It shows productivity gains but does not measure full costs against benefits in Q2 2024.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no realized, sector-wide Q2 2024 revenue and loss figures, only one firm's annual estimates. It has no cost-benefit deployment evidence for the period. Neither part of the claim is established or refuted.

attribution.note: Zitron's own analytic statement in his post.

semantics.note: 'Only when' is correctly kept as making inadequate returns a necessary condition for the plan failing. It is a general causal claim with no horizon.

contract.note: Reading 'only when' as a necessary condition is ordinary. The plan, its failure and adequate returns are not defined, so any result depends on the evaluator's reading.

evidence.note: CRS analysis, reproduced by EveryCRSReport, of antitrust concerns. It raises legal constraints as a possible alternative cause but records no actual failure of the strategy while returns were adequate.

reviews.rationale: The packet records no failure of the control strategy, and no evidence of returns or of what caused any outcome. The claimed necessary condition cannot be confirmed or refuted from the packet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own unqualified assertion in his post.

semantics.note: Faithful universal claim. The separate consequence ('effectively control every product') is rightly left out. 'No private startup' is unhedged.

contract.note: Counting a privately financed startup owned by a parent company, with substantial training and deployment, is an ordinary reading of 'private startup'. One clear counterexample is enough to contradict a universal claim.

evidence.note: Dated May 2024 paper: DeepSeek-V2, a 236B-parameter model, trained with an in-house framework on an H800 cluster and deployed, all before the post.
Later reporting (Nov 2024) that DeepSeek is fully funded by High-Flyer and uses High-Flyer's compute. It backs up independent financing but is not itself a record from the target period.
2025 testimony tracing DeepSeek's funding and infrastructure to its parent High-Flyer from 2023. It supports continuity of independent resources.

reviews.rationale: DeepSeek trained and deployed a large, competitive LLM before the post. It did so on its own cluster with financing from its parent, High-Flyer, and no help from Google, Amazon or Microsoft is shown. One counterexample defeats 'no private startup'. The weak point is that no audited supplier inventory is available.
